answer: Each identity must grow a crystal from a seed: its first payments go to partners drawn from clusters that do not already transact with each other, and the bond hardens only after that seed survives one audit round. Every new identity also burns one dose of saffron into its bond receipt; the k-th dose in a window costs k doses, so opening n identities burns n(n+1)/2. Auditors walk a spiral, doubling their inspection radius each round, which exposes any coalition whose counterparty set repeats. Faking thus needs partners that cannot be pooled plus an escalating dye, and neither can be resold.
